step1_summary.Chief complaint: Low energy, difficulty getting up in the morning, low mood, decreased sex drive over the past 2 months.
Symptoms: Onset: Around 2 months ago coinciding with starting a new job.
Severity: Significant fatigue impacting daily activities; difficulty focusing, distracted.
Associated symptoms: Difficulty sleeping (insomnia), low mood, decreased appetite, shortness of breath on exertion, decreased sex drive.
step1_summary.Family/social history: Father committed suicide 15 years ago; no other psychiatric or significant family history; married; employed; no social habits documented.
step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: Not documented in transcript; planned for in-person examination.
step1_summary.Labs/imaging: None performed yet; blood tests planned.

V: Chronic heart failure: Could explain fatigue, shortness of breath with exertion.
Anemia due to chronic disease: Could cause fatigue and breathlessness.
I: Chronic infection (e.g., viral hepatitis, tuberculosis): Can cause prolonged fatigue and low mood.
Hypothyroidism-related inflammation: Although stable on treatment, possible under-treatment causing symptoms.
N: Depression secondary to neoplasm (e.g., brain tumor): Rare but possible cause of mood changes and fatigue.
D: Hypothyroidism (under-treated or poorly controlled): Patient has hypothyroid history and is symptomatic despite treatment.
Vitamin D or B12 deficiency: Can cause fatigue, low mood, cognitive symptoms.
I2: Medication side effect from Thyroxine overdose or underdose: Can cause mood and energy changes.
Work-related stress or burnout (iatrogenic-like): Recent new job starting coinciding with symptom onset.
A: Autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto’s thyroiditis): Ongoing autoimmune process leading to hypothyroidism and mood symptoms.
E: Depression (Major depressive disorder): Key symptoms are fatigue, low mood, reduced concentration, decreased appetite and sex drive.
Sleep disorder (insomnia): Difficult sleeping contributing to fatigue and mood issues.
